FINAL BALANCE (tuned against the combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms telegraph as the Tier 0 anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms): 36 HP is about 5 light hits, same damage as the grunt, 500 ms wind-up so the wide sweep reads one beat slower. name: Rust Iron Line Cordon
description: A Rust grunt of the Iron Line in cheap rust-coated slate plating, a plain steel helmet with a cyan visor and no personal marks, because the helmets hide who they are. Same boxy, symmetrical build as the grunt, with a gunmetal push-bar held across the chest.
behaviour: Moves in at grunt speed and stops at the front of the group to hold the lane, trying to pin Zed against his own crowd. Uses one wide sweep with the push-bar that shoves Zed back along the lane. Counts against the attacker cap like any other attacker, and never attacks from behind. When Zed gets too close or grabs too often it answers with the grunt Helmet Headbutt (short wind-up, brief stun) from the GDD Iron Line move list.

weakness: Low health and a short reach in depth. Step out of the lane (dodge) or block the shove, then punish in the recovery window. Heavy attacks from the side skip its guard-stance and juggle it clear of the line.

name: Rust Breaker
description: A hulking Rust Bruiser in heavily reinforced slate and steel plating, with a massive squared-off silhouette, a small helmet and a cyan visor. Plants its feet and slams both braces into the floor, leaving a short patch of rattled ground in front of it that Zed should stay out of for a moment (area denial). Long recovery after every slam. GDD move list. 1) Gauntlet Smash: downward smash with a reinforced gauntlet, medium startup, causes ground bounce, breaks player block, signature thud on impact (this is the slam above). 2) Rust Uppercut: a rising punch that launches Zed and works as an anti-air option; used when Zed jumps too often. 3) Body Check: a shoulder slam with plated armour, a short forward dash that knocks Zed back, can interrupt combos, and has super armour during the dash.

Do not try to trade hits during the Body Check dash (super armour): sidestep it. Stop jumping in on it, or the Uppercut answers. Block does not hold against the Smash (it breaks block), so dodge it.
look: Hulking squared-off silhouette in heavy slate and steel plating, small helmet, cyan visor, gunmetal gauntlet brace on each forearm.

The moves and the 30 percent HP phase trigger are canon; every stat and wind-up below is proposed. GDD wording clashes with the tone rules in places (Rust described as executioners, "brutal"); this entry keeps Varr cold and official, and knocks Zed down rather than harming him lethally. Also: the GDD stance name "Antirush" is probably a typo and is recorded here as the anti-rush-down stance. FINAL BALANCE (tuned against the combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms telegraph as the Tier 0 anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms): 320 HP is about 18 finishers and the top of the curve (grunt 30, Breaker 90, Fang 140, Architect 160); 18 damage on the fast Authority Strike keeps Zed alive for at least 5 hits; 400 ms is the shortest boss wind-up, justified by the GDD "fast startup", and stays above the 300 ms floor. Phase 2 (30 percent HP): moveSpeed x1.15, recoverMs x0.8, damage unchanged, so "relentless" comes from tempo and drones, not one-shots. Numbers final.
name: Overseer Halden Varr
description: The founder of Rust and its Main Boss: a former military strategist who believed order could only be achieved through fear, and who replaced the city officials with Rust loyalists. Phase one: a crisp slate command coat over rust-coated plating, an electrified gauntlet on one fist and an emitter for an energy shield on the other arm, a tall cyan visor. Phase two: full oxidized armour, heavier and more boxy, with drones circling. Cold, symmetrical and official. Fought in the Corporate Tower command chamber.
behaviour: Two-phase final boss that fights alongside the units he calls. Phase 1, "Authority": Authority Strike (electrified gauntlet punch, high damage, knockback, fast startup); Command Shield (energy shield that blocks all frontal attacks and must be flanked or broken); Command Override (summons Rust Grunts, Watchers or Copper Fangs, Varr fights alongside them, counted against the attacker cap); Adaptive Counter (changes stance based on Zed's behaviour: anti-air stance if Zed jumps too often, anti-rush-down stance if Zed charges in, anti-combo stance if Zed strings long combos, forcing Zed to vary his play). Phase 2, "Rust Protocol", triggered at 30 percent HP: Hybrid Assault (uses moves from every Rust unit type: Breaker slam, Watcher taser shot, Copper Fang gauntlet combo and Overseer-style control attacks); Drone Command (summons elite drones that fire lasers in bullet-hell patterns); Rust Collapse super move (Varr overloads his armour for a massive area explosion, the arena walls electrify, and the final phase becomes relentless). Zed is knocked down and pushed back by these, never put down for good.
telegraph: Authority Strike: 400 ms wind-up, gauntlet drawn back and crackling. Command Shield: shield emitter glows and hums before it deploys, 500 ms. Command Override: 800 ms, console pulse rings mark where units appear. Adaptive Counter: a visible stance change with a colour cue (the stance is shown, never hidden). Drones: 600 ms lock-on line before each laser. Rust Collapse: a long 1500 ms charge, armour cracks glowing, a huge red ground danger zone, and the walls flash a warning before they electrify. Every attack keeps the red telegraph icon, scaled 1.4 times, with the standard tint and thicker outline.
weakness: Flank or break the Command Shield with heavy attacks; clear summoned units to focus Varr; vary the approach so Adaptive Counter never settles on one stance; in phase two dodge the Collapse zone and the drone lanes, then punish in the recovery. Rewards every pillar: combos, block, dodge, parry and wave-clearing under pressure.
look: Phase 1: crisp slate command coat over oxidized plating, electrified gauntlet on one fist, shield emitter on the other arm, tall cyan visor. Phase 2: full heavy boxy armour with circling drones.

description: A Rust Overseer of the rooftops, lean in a dark slate suit with a grapple launcher on each forearm and a slim cyan visor, much lighter than the other Overseers. Cold, symmetrical and boxy even when moving fast, with a faint cyan outline that stays visible when he turns semi-invisible.
behaviour: Phase 1, "Silent Hunter": GrappleDash Barrage (zips between platforms, attacking from above or from behind, very fast, hard to punish without prediction); Skyline Snare (throws electrified wire traps that restrict movement and can immobilise Zed briefly, forcing careful navigation); Silent Step (turns semi-invisible with only a faint outline, and his next attack is a guaranteed critical, used unpredictably); Rooftop Execution (a dive attack from above for high damage that creates a shockwave, punishing players who stay on the ground). Phase 2, "Ghost of the Skyline", at 50 percent HP (faster and quieter): Grapple Clone (afterimages left when he grapples perform fake attacks, while the real Silas attacks from an unexpected angle); Shadow Pulse (releases a burst of energy that knocks Zed back and resets spacing, used after combos); Vanish Storm super move (disappears completely, multiple silhouettes attack from all sides, and the real Silas finishes with a heavy strike; requires reading patterns). Zed is knocked down and pushed back, never put down for good.
telegraph: GrappleDash Barrage: 400 ms, the grapple line shows and a red marker lands at the destination platform. Skyline Snare: 600 ms, the wire glints and a red strip marks the trap. Silent Step: 500 ms shimmer, then the faint outline stays. The critical hit after Silent Step has its own 500 ms cyan flash. Rooftop Execution: 600 ms, a red shadow circle grows on the floor under the dive. Grapple Clone: 500 ms. Shadow Pulse: 450 ms ring. Vanish Storm: 1200 ms fade, silhouettes each get a red icon and the real one gets a heavier outline. All keep the red telegraph icon scaled 1.4 times.
weakness: Watch the red shadow under the dive and stay off the ground marker; check the outline during Silent Step and block or dodge the flashed critical. Keep moving through snares, hit the real Silas (the one with the heavier outline) and punish him after Shadow Pulse resets spacing.
look: Lean dark slate suit, grapple launcher on each forearm, slim cyan visor; much lighter than the other Overseers; faint cyan outline remains when semi-invisible.

name: Overseer Dr. Maren Holt
description: A Rust Overseer of the undercity lab in a slate lab coat over light plating, a rebreather and a cyan visor, a belt of chemical vials and a dart launcher on one forearm. Cold, symmetrical and official; her suit glows with pressure in the second phase. Purple and green fog marks her gas.
behaviour: Phase 1, "Chemical Control": Fear Gas (releases purple fog that distorts Zed's controls and blurs the screen, forcing careful movement); Obedience Mist (green fog that slows movement, reduces dodge distance and makes combos harder); Toxin Burst (throws chemical vials that create lingering area damage zones, controlling space); Sedative Shot (fires a dart that reduces Zed's attack speed, used to punish aggressive players). Phase 2, "Doctor's Orders", at 40 percent HP (suit glows with chemical pressure): NeuroFog (the whole arena fills with fog, Zed's vision is reduced, Holt becomes harder to track and uses stealth attacks); Corrosive Wave (throws a large vial that explodes into spreading acid that damages both Zed and Holt, forcing repositioning); Compliance Protocol super move (releases a massive chemical cloud, Zed's controls reverse, damage over time, and Holt becomes extremely aggressive). Effects ease off when Zed clears the fog; Zed is knocked down and pushed back, never put down for good.
telegraph: Fear Gas: 700 ms vent hiss and purple puff. Obedience Mist: 700 ms green puff. Toxin Burst: 600 ms, red ground circle where the vial lands. Sedative Shot: 450 ms, a thin line to Zed. NeuroFog: 900 ms, vents glow before the fog rolls in. Corrosive Wave: 700 ms, a red spreading-radius preview. Compliance Protocol: 1500 ms charge, a huge cloud outline and a "controls reversed" icon on the HUD before it reaches Zed. All keep the red telegraph icon scaled 1.4 times.
weakness: Stay out of the lingering zones and clear the fog by moving upwind of the vents. Do not over-commit while slowed or sedated; block or dodge the dart. Use Corrosive Wave against Holt by herding her into the acid, and learn the reversed controls during Compliance Protocol.
look: Slate lab coat over light plating, rebreather and cyan visor, belt of chemical vials, dart launcher on one forearm; purple and green fog marks her gas.

name: Rust Surveillance Drone
description: A small Rust surveillance drone summoned by Overseer Voss. Boxy, symmetrical, one cyan lens.
look: Small boxy slate drone with a single cyan lens, a short taser prong underneath and no markings; hovers at head height.
behaviour: Orbits Voss in a loose ring (3 to 5 at a time) and fires small taser bolts at Zed when it holds an attacker slot; counts against the attacker cap. telegraph: 600 ms: the cyan ring flashes at spawn, then the lens charges and the red telegraph icon pops above it before each bolt.
weakness: Fragile: any light attack or a juggle pops it. Clear drones to break the bullet-hell pressure and open a path to Voss.
